svg.title: Five layers between a model's SQL and the data, and which two are enforcement
svg.desc: Five rows of the same size are stacked in the order a statement meets them, with an arrow running down the left edge past all of them. The top three carry a chip reading Filter, are drawn with dashed outlines and a sieve glyph, and live in the server's security module: a parse and tree walk with sqlglot at the postgres dialect, a sixteen-name dangerous-function blocklist matched on the tree, and a required LIMIT with a ceiling of one thousand rows. The bottom two carry a chip reading Enforcement, are drawn with heavy solid outlines and a filled wall glyph, and live in PostgreSQL: the login role mcp_readonly granted SELECT and nothing else, and a thirty second statement timeout set on the role rather than on the pool. Beside every row, including the two that enforce, is the honest limit of that layer: no grammar covers all of PostgreSQL and unknown syntax becomes an opaque node no check can see inside; a blocklist only names what was dangerous the day it was written; a LIMIT bounds rows and never cost; a grant is only as narrow as the grants, and permits any SELECT including one that reads every customer record; and thirty seconds of load still happens before the backend kills the query. A closing line states that layers one to three are opinions about a string while layers four and five are grants on a login role, enforced whether this server is right or not.
svg.text: Five layers. Three are opinions, two are grants.
A statement enters at the top. Only the bottom two still hold if the top three are wrong.
LAYER
THE HONEST LIMIT
Filter
in the server, in security.py. Each one can be wrong.
Enforcement
in PostgreSQL. A grant is not a heuristic.
1 · Parse and walk the tree
sqlglot, dialect="postgres"
No grammar covers all of PostgreSQL. Unknown syntax
becomes an opaque node, and no check sees inside it.
2 · Function blocklist
16 names, matched on the tree
A blocklist names what was dangerous the day it was
written. Extensions ship more, and it never updates.
3 · LIMIT required, capped
ceiling 1000 rows, clamps
Bounds rows, never cost. A three-way self join returns
1000 rows and pins a replica for as long as it takes.
4 · Role mcp_readonly
GRANT SELECT, and nothing else
Only as narrow as the grants. It permits any SELECT,
including one that reads every customer record.
5 · statement_timeout 30s
set on the role, not the pool
Thirty seconds of load still happens before the backend
kills it. Set it lower than you think you need.
Layers 1 to 3 are opinions about a string. Layers 4 and 5 are grants on a login role, enforced whether this server is right or not.
